prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury attorney for every Chicago car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case, the seriousness of injuries, whether the case may go to trial, and what kind of communication/fee arrangement you prefer. I can help you find the best lawyer for your situation. First, here’s how to pick one and some reputable Chicago names you can consider.

How to pick the right attorney
- Look for specialization: pick lawyers or firms that focus on car-accident/personal-injury work (not general practice).
- Relevant experience: ask about experience with cases like yours (serious injury, catastrophic, wrongful death, multiple-vehicle, uninsured motorist, hit-and-run).
- Track record: settlements/verdicts and whether the attorney tries cases in court (trial experience matters if the insurer won’t pay).
- Resources: firms that can advance costs for medical records, experts, accident reconstruction if needed.
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (commonly ~33% to 40% of recovery); confirm who pays costs if you lose.
- Communication and availability: get a clear point of contact and expected timelines.
- Reputation and reviews: check client reviews, Avvo/Martindale-Hubbell ratings, Super Lawyers listings, and local bar complaints.

Interview questions to ask during a free consult
- Have you handled cases like mine? What was the result?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your fee and how are expenses handled?
- Do you take cases to trial? How many jury trials have you done?
- What kind of recovery should I reasonably expect and what is the timeline?
- How often will you update me?

Practical steps right now
- Get prompt medical care and follow all treatment — treatment records are key evidence.
- Report the crash to police and get a copy of the report.
- Preserve photos, witness contact info, and any dashcam/phone footage.
- Don’t give recorded statements or sign releases from the insurer without consulting an attorney.

Important legal notes
- Illinois generally has a 2-year statute of limitations for personal injury claims from the date of the accident (there are exceptions — government claims, minors, etc.), so don’t delay contacting an attorney.
- Contingency fee is typical, so many injury attorneys will evaluate your case with no upfront fee.

Well-known Chicago personal-injury firms (examples to consider)
These are some firms historically known for car-accident and personal-injury work in Chicago (verify current availability/reputation when you contact them):
- Clifford Law Offices
- Corboy & Demetrio
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard
- Levin & Perconti
- Power Rogers & Smith

If you want, I can:
- Narrow this to a short list that’s a good match for your case if you tell me your neighborhood/ZIP, what injuries you sustained, whether the other driver admitted fault, and whether insurers are already involved.
- Draft a list of documents to bring to your first consultation.
